speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand your infant is experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. Can you describe the specific activities or positions that seem to trigger these episodes, such as feeding or lying on their back?

speaker: Patient
text: 10-month-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. The mother notes that the wheezing exacerbates when the child is crying, feeding, and when his neck is flexed. Additionally, there are instances where the child vomits after feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for that information. The exacerbation with neck flexion and feeding is very suggestive of a vascular or structural issue in the neck. Has he had any episodes of cyanosis or apnea, and does the stridor sound biphasic (both inspiratory and expiratory) or primarily inspiratory?

REQUEST TEST: Neck Ultrasound

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal neck ultrasound makes a vascular ring less likely, so I need to explore other causes. Does the stridor improve when his neck is extended, and has he had any history of intubation or recent respiratory infections?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Recurrent episodes of stridor and wheezing. I also have Exacerbation during crying, Exacerbation during feeding, Exacerbation with neck flexion, Relief with neck extension, Occasional vomiting post-feeding.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The relief with neck extension and exacerbation with flexion strongly suggests laryngomalacia, but the vomiting and wheezing raise concern for GERD or a vascular ring missed by ultrasound. Has he experienced any "barking" cough or hoarseness, and has a chest X-ray been performed to rule out compression of the airway or esophagus?

REQUEST TEST: Chest_X-Ray
